presets.about: Domini — the Lord's, as in Anno Domini: every date the world writes is counted as the Year of the Lord, and this dial wears that name. DOMY is the dark watch of the pair: the shadowed cross of Fear, Anger, Hate and Suffering, walked through the night so the day can be walked free. The name is the word Domini bent into a wheel — the Lord's own hours, kept even in the dark.

reading.text: the dark path's fourth and last station (DOMY, 12h): what fermented all night stands exposed in full noon light. "Nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest" (Luke 8:17) — the dark path does not end in relief, it ends SEEN.
reading.title: SUFFERING

reading.text: the dark path's first station (DOMY, 20h): the panic that seizes before the mind can weigh the danger, Ysteria's own root — the body deciding before the will does. "The thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).
reading.title: FEAR

reading.text: the dark path's second station (DOMY, 24h): wrath kept past sundown, the LIVID hour — lividus, Latin for bruise-purple, the color rage leaves on the skin and on the night. "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Ephesians 4:26) — this station is what happens when it does.
reading.title: ANGER

reading.text: the dark path's third station (DOMY, 4h): anger gone cold and decided, no longer a flare but a verdict held before dawn. "He that hateth his brother is in darkness" (1 John 2:11) — the hour before light is where the verdict is signed.
reading.title: HATE

12.name: M — Misery
12.reading:
Suffering — the dark path's last station: M for Miseria, Latin for wretchedness. At noon what fermented in the dark stands naked in full light — "nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest" (Luke 8:17); and the Passion itself darkened noon: "from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land" (Matthew 27:45).

Down the spine: Ω — Suffering against Anger; the dark path ends EXPOSED before the Judge at noon (the chiasm of the Two Crosses).

M is the 13th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, no relation to its noon seat; it stands here for Miseria, not for its ordinal.

20.name: Y — Ysteria
20.reading:
Fear — the dark path's first station, at dusk on the future's red arm: Y for Ysteria (Greek ὑστέρα — the panic that seizes and unmans) and for the Yips, the fear that blocks the hand at the decisive moment. "The thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).

Across the crossbar: D — Fear against Hate, the panic of dusk facing the cold decision of the hour before dawn.

Y is the 25th letter of the modern Latin alphabet (22nd of the 23-letter classical Latin row that omits J, U, W) — neither number is 20; Y sits at 20h for Ysteria's initial, not for any ordinal claim.

24.name: Ω — Orge
24.reading:
Anger — the midnight station: Ω for Orgē (ὀργή — wrath, the anger that keeps), at the LIVID hour — lividus is Latin for bruise-purple and for rage. Ephesians 4:26 broken: the sun went down upon the wrath, and midnight found it awake.

Up the spine: M — Anger against Suffering: what midnight wrath ferments, noon will expose (Luke 8:17).

Ω is the 24th and last letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 24th hour — the one true ordinal match on this card, shared with LOOP's own Ω.

4.name: D — Detest
4.reading:
Hate — the station before dawn: D for Detestatio, the Latin curse of loathing — anger cooled into cold, decided hate on the past's blue arm; Judas's own hour, the kiss by night. "He that hateth his brother… walketh in darkness" (1 John 2:11).

Across the crossbar: Y — Hate against Fear, the frozen grudge facing the panic that first bred it.

D is the 4th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, seated exactly on the 4th hour — its ordinal and its station word (Detestatio) agree by the same coincidence that seats M elsewhere on this card.

presets.name: DOMY

presets.about: The loop has no end — that is its whole theology. Twenty-four hours joined in a ring; Omega, the letter of endings, bent here into O, a circle that cannot end; the light cross of Faith, Love, Hope and Salvation, whose last station at midnight hands the wheel back to the first at dawn. Read the four seats aloud and they say the name: L-Ω-Ω-Π — LOOP, the day without end, world without end.

reading.text: the light path's second station and the crown of the four (LOOP, 12h): the work done for others — Leitourgia, service as deed rather than sentiment, held at noon in full light where it costs the most. Love is the only one of the three that must be ACTUAL to exist at all. "Let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth" (1 John 3:18).
reading.title: LOVE

reading.text: the light path's third station (LOOP, 16h): the watch kept for what has not arrived — Prosdokia, expectation with its eyes open. It takes the hour the light begins to leave, because in the morning you can SEE the sun and need no hope for it, and it stands last before the summit because the thing it reaches for IS salvation. "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul" (Hebrews 6:19).
reading.title: HOPE

reading.text: the light path's fourth and last station (LOOP, 24h): the help that delivers, arriving at the identical midnight hour DOMY's Anger keeps — the same clock face, the opposite outcome. "At midnight Paul and Silas prayed… and all the doors were opened" (Acts 16:25–26).
reading.title: SALVATION

reading.text: the light path's first station (LOOP, 8h): the foundation stone laid before anything can be built on it — Themelios, what is RECEIVED at the start of the road rather than invented at it. Faith answers something already given, which is why it stands where the day begins. "Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen" (Hebrews 11:1).
reading.title: FAITH

12.name: L — Leitourgia
12.note: lang-ok: Greek etymology quotation in parentheses beside its English gloss — the sealed legend convention of every reading in this file (CANON.md §The Cross Rings)
12.reading:
Love — the noon station and the crown of the four: L for Leitourgia (λειτουργία — the work done for the people), service as deed rather than sentiment, and for Loyalty, yellow noon's own virtue. Love is the only one of the three that must be ACTUAL to exist at all, held in full light where it costs the most. "Let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth" (1 John 3:18).

Down the spine: Ω — Love against Salvation: what is served in daylight is delivered at midnight (the chiasm of the Two Crosses).

L is the 12th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, seated exactly on the 12th hour/noon — an ordinal match (Λ, the Greek equivalent, is the 11th letter, not the 12th): the one seat that breaks the ring's Greek arithmetic now holds the one virtue that does not end.

16.name: Π — Prosdokia
16.note: lang-ok: Greek etymology quotation in parentheses beside its English gloss — the sealed legend convention of every reading in this file (CANON.md §The Cross Rings)
16.reading:
Hope — the vigor arm's station: Π for Prosdokia (προσδοκία — expectation), the watch kept for what has not arrived, eyes open toward evening. It takes the hour the light begins to leave — in the morning you can SEE the sun and need no hope for it — and it stands last before the summit because the thing it reaches for IS salvation. "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul" (Hebrews 6:19).

Across the crossbar: Θ — Hope against Faith, the watch still kept at evening facing the stone already laid at morning.

Π is the 16th letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 16th hour — an ordinal match.

24.name: Ω — Opheleia
24.reading:
Salvation — the light's ending in the dark's own hour: Ω for Ōpheleia (ὠφέλεια — the help that delivers) and for Omega itself, completion. "At midnight Paul and Silas prayed… and all the doors were opened" (Acts 16:25–26).

Up the spine: L — Salvation against Love; the light path ends REMADE in the Creator's hands at midnight (2 Corinthians 5:17).

Ω is the 24th and last letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 24th hour — the same match DOMY's Ω carries.

8.name: Θ — Themelios
8.note: lang-ok: Greek etymology quotation in parentheses beside its English gloss — the sealed legend convention of every reading in this file (CANON.md §The Cross Rings)
8.reading:
Faith — the light path's first station, on Renewal's green: Θ for Themelios (θεμέλιος — the foundation stone), what is laid before anything can be built on it. Faith answers something ALREADY GIVEN — testimony, promise, event — which is why it stands where the day begins. "Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen" (Hebrews 11:1).

Across the crossbar: Π — Faith against Hope, the stone already laid at morning facing the watch still kept at evening.

Θ is the 8th letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 8th hour — an ordinal match.

presets.name: LOOP

presets.about: The denomination itself: E PLURIBUS UNUM — out of many, one. Out of twenty-four hours, one wheel; out of seven numbered seats, one letter — Ω at midnight, where the count ends and the day is one again. The dial stripped to pure count, and the count's one exception; its crown keeps your own hour and your own city.

12.name: 12 — The Noon
12.reading:
The present — the Judge's hour: TODAY, and nothing else. The dial's time doctrine holds that the past never existed and the future never comes; noon is the hour that says so in full light. "This is the day which the LORD hath made" (Psalm 118:24).

Down the axis: Ω — the present against The One who holds all of time; the day's height facing the deep that begins and completes it (Revelation 1:8).

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

15.name: 15 — The Afternoon
15.reading:
The working hour — the day's labor carried onto its far slope: "man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening" (Psalm 104:23). The card of hours needs no emblem here; the number is the work itself, counted.

Across the wheel: 3 — the working afternoon against the souls' still hour; the hand at its task facing the deep where no hand moves.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

18.name: 18 — The Evening Frontier
18.reading:
Day meets night — the frontier hour. The Hebrew day BEGINS at sunset — "the evening and the morning were the first day" (Genesis 1:5) — so this frontier is a beginning worn as an ending.

Across the wheel: 6 — evening against dawn, the two frontiers of the night: one closes the light, the other gives it back.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

21.name: 21 — The Vesper Hour
21.reading:
The feast and the rest after work — the Rose's own hour, love's red thinned by moonlight. What the afternoon earned, the vesper hour enjoys and lays down: "he giveth his beloved sleep" (Psalm 127:2).

Across the wheel: 9 — the vesper rest against the climbing morning; the day laid down facing the day picking itself up.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

24.name: Ω — The One
24.reading:
Where the count would close at 24 stands the letter that closes the alphabet: "I am Alpha and Omega… which is, and which was, and which is to come" (Revelation 1:8) — the definition of The One — with Exodus 3:14, I AM THAT I AM, the name spoken by itself. On the card of hours the midnight seat is the one hour no number can say: the hour that ends one day and begins the next is not a count but a completion. E PLURIBUS UNUM — out of many hours, one wheel.

Up the axis: 12 — The One against the noon it judges from; the deep that holds all of time facing the hour that can only hold today.

Ω is the 24th and last letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 24th hour where the day's count would otherwise run out of numbers — the one glyph on this card that is not a number, closing the alphabet where the clock closes the day.

3.name: 3 — The Souls' Hour
3.reading:
The deep of night — the Ages wheel's Unborn wedge pools here: the ancestors and the not-yet-born in one moonlight community, the sea a soul comes from and returns to. The only hour awake with nothing but the stars: "when I consider thy heavens… the moon and the stars" (Psalm 8:3).

Across the wheel: 15 — the still hour against the working afternoon; the community of souls facing the single pair of hands at its task.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

6.name: 6 — The New Morning
6.reading:
Rebirth without the past — the finished night needs no more thought. "His compassions fail not. They are new every morning" (Lamentations 3:22–23).

Across the wheel: 18 — dawn against evening: the frontier that returns the light facing the frontier that surrendered it.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

9.name: 9 — The Climbing Morning
9.reading:
Life rising toward noon — spring's own green in the Rose, the day on its most alive climb. "In the morning sow thy seed" (Ecclesiastes 11:6): the morning hour is the sowing hour, because everything it does still has the whole day to grow in.

Across the wheel: 21 — the climb against the rest; seed-time facing the feast.

No ordinal line: this seat wears the hour itself as the glyph, so the numeral and its "ordinal" are the same fact stated once; an ordinal sentence here would just repeat the station name.

presets.name: The One

presets.about: The order founded to guard Jerusalem still keeps its watch here: four crosses, four watches — noon, evening, midnight, morning — the same vigil under every light, the Beauceant's black-over-white worn as a day and a night. The crown ticks the hour of Jerusalem, the city of the vow, under the order's own motto: NON NOBIS DOMINE — not unto us, O Lord, but unto Thy name give glory.

reading.text: "Not unto us, O Lord." The opening of Psalm 115:1 (Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam — "not unto us, but unto thy name, give glory") and the Knights Templar's own battle motto: a vow of no personal credit sworn by men who fought and died for it — the order's whole ethic compressed into five words borrowed from a psalm older than the order by two thousand years.
reading.title: NON NOBIS DOMINE

12.name: ✠ — The Noon Watch
12.reading:
The cross at zenith — duty kept in full light: "walk while ye have the light" (John 12:35). Four crosses ring this card and the glyph never changes — only the hour does; the card's whole doctrine is constancy under changing light, the vigil that does not pick its weather.

Down the spine: the Midnight Watch — the same cross in all of the light and in none of it.

No ordinal line: the cross pattée is a symbol, not a letter, and repeats unchanged at all four seats — the card's whole doctrine is that the glyph does NOT vary, only the station does, so an ordinal comparison has nothing to attach to.

18.name: ✠ — The Evening Watch
18.reading:
The frontier post where day meets night: "abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent" (Luke 24:29). The order's banner was the Beauceant, black over white — a duality worn as cloth — and this is the hour its two fields touch.

Across the crossbar: the Morning Watch — the watch that hands the light away facing the watch that receives it back.

No ordinal line: the cross pattée is a symbol, not a letter, and repeats unchanged at all four seats — the card's whole doctrine is that the glyph does NOT vary, only the station does, so an ordinal comparison has nothing to attach to.

24.name: ✠ — The Midnight Watch
24.reading:
The watch kept when every other light is out: "at midnight there was a cry made… behold, the bridegroom cometh" (Matthew 25:6). The vigil hour proves the vigil: anyone stands guard at noon.

Up the spine: the Noon Watch — the same cross, the opposite weather.

No ordinal line: the cross pattée is a symbol, not a letter, and repeats unchanged at all four seats — the card's whole doctrine is that the glyph does NOT vary, only the station does, so an ordinal comparison has nothing to attach to.

6.name: ✠ — The Morning Watch
6.reading:
The relieved watch: "weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning" (Psalm 30:5). The night's watch ends not in relief but in renewal — the wheel hands the vigil back to the first watch.

Across the crossbar: the Evening Watch — the receiving frontier facing the surrendering one.

No ordinal line: the cross pattée is a symbol, not a letter, and repeats unchanged at all four seats — the card's whole doctrine is that the glyph does NOT vary, only the station does, so an ordinal comparison has nothing to attach to.

presets.name: Templar

presets.about: The Great Seal of the one-dollar bill, laid on the wheel: the Eye of Providence above the crown, the mottos of the unfinished pyramid arcing outside. The most-held object on Earth carries the oldest symbols of the newest empire — and between Judge and Creator, Accuser and Advocate, this dial spells what the bill only hints.

reading.text: "He has favored our undertakings." The shorter half of the Great Seal's reverse motto, adapted from Virgil's Aeneid (IX.625, audacibus annue coeptis — "look with favor on this bold endeavor"): a prayer, not a boast — the Eye of Providence is asked to bless the work, the work does not claim to have earned it on its own.
reading.title: ANNUIT COEPTIS

reading.text: "A new order of the ages." The longer half of the same motto, drawn from Virgil's Fourth Eclogue (magnus ab integro saeclorum nascitur ordo — "the great line of the centuries begins anew"): not a new order built to replace the old by force, but a new age understood to have already begun — the pyramid's unfinished top, a work still under construction.
reading.title: NOVUS ORDO SECLORUM

12.name: 👁 — The Eye of Providence
12.reading:
God as JUDGE — the Eye of Providence over the crown, the office that watches and weighs: "the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth" (2 Chronicles 16:9). On the Cube this is the high seat of the judgment hinge: judgment by BOND — Loyalty in measure, Tribalism past it.

Across the wheel: Ω — the Judge against the Creator, the weighing above facing the making below (Revelation 1:8; Genesis 1:1).

No ordinal line: the Eye of Providence is a pictogram, not a letter, and carries no position in any alphabet to compare against noon.

16.name: S — Satanic Scourge
16.reading:
the Devil as DESTROYER — the Satanic Scourge, the force that wastes what it cannot own, on the vigor arm: where the Accuser is judicial evil, the Scourge is destructive evil. On the Cube: STORM — Vigor that has lost direction, the fall of Frenzy.

Across the wheel: N — the Scourge against the Advocate, the unmaking hand facing the defending word (the Double Trinity's Advocate ↔ Destroyer diagonal).

S is the 19th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, no relation to its 16h seat; it stands here for Sigma/Satanic Scourge, not for its ordinal.

20.name: M — Malignant Accuser
20.reading:
the Devil as PROSECUTOR — the Malignant Accuser who indicts the soul: "the accuser of our brethren" (Revelation 12:10); diabolos itself means the slanderer. On the Cube: MEGALOMANIA — Dignity enthroned as divinity, Lucifer's own fall: "I will ascend into heaven" (Isaiah 14:13).

Across the wheel: A — the Accuser against the Aegis, the charge brought facing the shield raised (Prosecutor ↔ Preserver).

M is the 13th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, no relation to its 20h seat; it stands here for Master/Malignant Accuser, not for its ordinal.

24.name: Ω — Omnific Originator
24.reading:
God as CREATOR — the Omnific Originator, the all-creating: he does not guard, defend, accuse or destroy what exists; he gives existence to existence itself (Ho On, "the One Who Is"; Revelation 1:8). On the Cube Ω is the judgment hinge entire: OBLIGATION — to whom or to what am I bound? Loyalty ↔ Integrity in measure, Tribalism ↔ Legalism past it.

Across the wheel: 👁 — the Creator against the Judge, the making below facing the weighing above (Revelation 1:8; Genesis 1:1).

Ω is the 24th and last letter of the Greek alphabet, seated exactly on the 24th hour — the same match every other Ω seat on this dial carries.

4.name: N — Nazarene Advocate
4.reading:
Jesus as ADVOCATE — the Nazarene Advocate who answers the charge: "we have an advocate with the Father" (1 John 2:1); he does not deny the sin, he stands beside the sinner. On the Cube: NUMBNESS — Composure emptied of life, the fall of Lethargy, the sleeping watch (Matthew 26:40).

Across the wheel: S — the Advocate against the Scourge, the defending word facing the unmaking hand (the Double Trinity's Advocate ↔ Destroyer diagonal).

N is the 14th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, no relation to its 4h seat; it stands here for Nazarene, not for its ordinal.

8.name: A — Anointed Aegis
8.reading:
Jesus as GUARDIAN — the Anointed Aegis, the shield that takes the blow: the Guardian protects from attack as the Advocate defends from accusation; the Preserver's own green arm (Hebrews 1:14). On the Cube: ABNEGATION — Humility turned against the self, the fall of Self-Annihilation, Judas's green fall.

Across the wheel: M — the Aegis against the Accuser, the shield raised facing the charge brought (Prosecutor ↔ Preserver).

A is the 1st letter of the modern Latin alphabet (and of the Greek), no relation to its 8h seat; it stands here for Alpha/Aegis, not for its ordinal.

presets.name: Dollar

presets.about: Chi — the letter the cosmos is written in. Plato taught that the Maker crossed the two great circles of heaven 'in the shape of the letter Χ' — and every equinox redraws that X where the sun's road crosses the sky's equator. On the horizon the four solstice suns rise and set on its arms; on the wheel the 24th letter stands alone at the 24th hour: the initial of Christós, the sign in which Constantine conquered, the saltire of the first-called apostle, the unknown with which every unlettered soul still signs.

reading.text: the fish. A Greek acrostic, not a word chosen for its shape: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς Θεοῦ Υἱὸς Σωτήρ, "Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior" — each of the five letters opens one clause of the confession, and only when read together do they also spell the fish early Christians drew in secret as a recognition mark.
reading.title: ΙΧΘΥΣ

reading.text: "In this sign, conquer." The words Constantine reported seeing beside a cross of light before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge (Eusebius, Life of Constantine I.28) — THIS sign being the Chi-Rho, the first two Greek letters of Χριστός overlaid; the labarum built from the vision carried the sentence into battle and, after the victory, into the empire's own standard.
reading.title: IN HOC SIGNO VINCES

24.name: X — Chi
24.reading:
The 24th and final letter of the classical Greek alphabet — the Latin alphabet's own 24th letter, X, inherits the seat, so on the 24th hour this card seats the Latin twin of the Ω every other bundled preset already keeps there. Plato's Timaeus (36b) has the Maker cross the two great circles of heaven "in the shape of the letter Χ": the ecliptic and the celestial equator, whose two crossings are the equinoxes this dial pins at 90°/270°.

It is also the initial of Χριστός — the Chi-Rho at the heart of ΙΧΘΥΣ and of IN HOC SIGNO VINCES, the sentence this same card carries in its own two crown arcs; and, in Rome, X was simply ten — the Decalogue's own count.

X is the 24th letter of the modern Latin alphabet, seated exactly on the 24th hour — the Latin twin of Ω's own match on the identical seat, on a different card.

presets.name: CHI
